editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the Open Plan session caveat in [22] and the parameter-value requirement in [3]. Some terms are rendered inconsistently. "primitive" stays in English in [0] but is "primitif" everywhere else, and "circuit" switches between "Circuit" ([3], [20], [24]) and "sirkuit" ([18], [19]). One sentence is also a calque: [22] puts "masing-masing" at the end, copying the English "respectively", and a native writer would put it earlier in the sentence.

examples.source: how to use the IBM Quantum Sampler primitive
examples.translation: cara menggunakan primitive IBM Quantum Sampler
examples.suggested: cara menggunakan primitif Sampler IBM Quantum
examples.why: Everywhere else in the file this is 'primitif', so the English 'primitive' here is inconsistent.

examples.source: You need at least one circuit as the input to the Sampler primitive.
examples.translation: Kamu membutuhkan setidaknya satu sirkuit sebagai input ke primitif Sampler.
examples.suggested: Pick one form ('sirkuit') and use it throughout the file
examples.why: 'sirkuit' ([18], [19]) and 'Circuit' ([3], [20], [24]) both appear for the same concept.

examples.source: Possible values are `batch`, `session`, or `backend` objects for batch, session, and job execution mode, respectively.
examples.translation: Nilai yang mungkin adalah objek `batch`, `session`, atau `backend` untuk mode eksekusi batch, session, dan job, masing-masing.
examples.suggested: Nilai yang mungkin adalah objek `batch`, `session`, atau `backend`, masing-masing untuk mode eksekusi batch, session, dan job.
examples.why: Putting 'masing-masing' at the end of the sentence copies the English word order and reads stiff in Indonesian.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The Bell-state claims in [35], the independent-vs-correlated expectation values in [51] and the resilience-level trade-off in [60] all come through correctly, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are editorial. The page switches between "Anda" and "kamu"/"-mu", sometimes inside a single paragraph ([41], [48]). "Entangled/entanglement" is rendered two ways: "terjalin" in [29] and [35], but "keterikatan kuantum" in [51]. Two smaller slips: "post-process" in [48] is flattened to plain "memproses", and "robust programs" in [6] becomes "program yang jauh lebih kuat".

examples.source: so you usually collect a sample of the outputs ... You can estimate the value of the observable
examples.translation: jadi biasanya Anda mengumpulkan sampel ... Kamu bisa memperkirakan nilai observabel
examples.suggested: jadi biasanya Anda mengumpulkan sampel ... Anda bisa memperkirakan nilai observabel
examples.why: The paragraph switches between Anda and kamu from one sentence to the next. The page should settle on one form of address.

examples.source: This is a hallmark of quantum entanglement.
examples.translation: Ini adalah ciri khas keterikatan kuantum.
examples.suggested: Ini adalah ciri khas keterjalinan kuantum.
examples.why: Earlier entries ([29], [35]) use 'terjalin' for entangled. Switching to 'keterikatan' here breaks the link a learner should make back to the Bell-state explanation.

examples.source: where you might post-process your results using, for example, measurement error mitigation
examples.translation: tempat Anda bisa memproses hasilmu menggunakan, misalnya, mitigasi error pengukuran
examples.suggested: tempat Anda bisa melakukan pasca-pemrosesan hasil menggunakan, misalnya, mitigasi error pengukuran
examples.why: The 'post-' is dropped, so the step no longer says the processing happens after execution. Step 4 of the second section ([61]) uses 'Pasca-proses', so using the same term here would keep them consistent.

examples.source: actual quantum research requires much more robust programs
examples.translation: penelitian kuantum nyata membutuhkan program yang jauh lebih kuat
examples.suggested: penelitian kuantum sesungguhnya membutuhkan program yang jauh lebih tangguh/kompleks
examples.why: 'Kuat' (strong) is a loose fit for 'robust' here, where the English means larger and more substantial. 'Tangguh' or 'kompleks' reads more naturally.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing here would mislead a learner, but there are a few small slips. In [10] and [16], "quantum Circuit" keeps the English word order, while [19] correctly says "Circuit kuantum". The file also switches register, using "Anda" in [5] but "hasilmu" in [20]. In [17], "high-fidelity" became the generic "berkualitas tinggi", which loses the technical term "fidelitas".

examples.source: Build a quantum circuit in under two minutes
examples.translation: Bangun quantum Circuit dalam waktu kurang dari dua menit
examples.suggested: Bangun Circuit kuantum dalam waktu kurang dari dua menit
examples.why: This keeps the English modifier order. Indonesian puts the modifier after the noun, as [19] already does with 'Circuit kuantum'. The same slip appears in [16].

examples.source: Refine your results
examples.translation: Sempurnakan hasilmu
examples.suggested: Sempurnakan hasil Anda
examples.why: [5] addresses the reader as 'Anda', but this entry switches to 'kamu' ('-mu'), so the page mixes two ways of addressing the reader.

examples.source: Construct high-fidelity circuits with reduced depth
examples.translation: Buat Circuit berkualitas tinggi dengan kedalaman yang lebih kecil
examples.suggested: Buat Circuit berfidelitas tinggi dengan kedalaman yang lebih kecil
examples.why: 'Fidelity' is a technical metric in quantum computing. The generic 'berkualitas tinggi' (high quality) loses that term, though it does not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The optional/required caveats, the version warnings and the Windows troubleshooting steps all match the English. The problems are small polish items. Footnote [14] ends with a stray ")" that is not in the source. "compiler" is written as "Compiler" in [10], [81] and [85] but as "Kompiler" in [31] and the MSVC accordion title in [37]. "from source" becomes "dari source" in [10] but "dari sumber" in [61] and [81]. Other pairs also switch within the file: "C header"/"header C", "snippet"/"cuplikan kode" and "situs"/"website". In [49], "beri komentar pada baris kode" is a stiff rendering of "comment out"; "jadikan komentar baris kode" reads more naturally.

examples.source: or simply install Make; it's not too late.
examples.translation: atau cukup instal Make; belum terlambat.)
examples.suggested: atau cukup instal Make; belum terlambat.
examples.why: A stray closing parenthesis was added that is not in the source and has no matching opening parenthesis.

examples.source: A C compiler: Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC)
examples.translation: Kompiler C: Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC)
examples.suggested: Compiler C: Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC)
examples.why: Inconsistent term. [10], [81] and [85] use "Compiler"; [31] and the [37] accordion title use "Kompiler". Pick one spelling for the whole page.

examples.source: avoids compiling `qiskit-aer` from source
examples.translation: menghindari kompilasi `qiskit-aer` dari sumber
examples.suggested: menghindari kompilasi `qiskit-aer` dari source
examples.why: [10] keeps "dari source" while [61] and [81] use "dari sumber" for the same idea. Use one rendering throughout.

examples.source: comment out the code lines that install Python 3.12
examples.translation: beri komentar pada baris kode yang menginstal Python 3.12
examples.suggested: jadikan komentar baris kode yang menginstal Python 3.12
examples.why: "beri komentar pada" can be read as annotating the lines rather than disabling them. "jadikan komentar" (or "comment out") is the usual phrasing among Indonesian developers.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The tricky condition in [29], "does not match both", is rendered correctly as "jumlah parameter atau jumlah qubit-nya tidak cocok", and [22] quietly fixes the English typo ("exported by our importer" becomes "exporter kita"). There are two minor issues. First, [54] uses "sirkuit" while the rest of the file keeps "Circuit", and [30] writes "gate dasar" in lowercase while the file otherwise writes "Gate". Second, the list items in the Recommendations admonition [58] are indented by four spaces, which the English does not have and which could render as a code block in MDX.

examples.source: they accept a circuit and, only in the case of qasm2.dump(), a location
examples.translation: mereka menerima sebuah sirkuit dan, hanya untuk qasm2.dump(), lokasi
examples.suggested: fungsi-fungsi ini menerima sebuah Circuit dan, khusus untuk qasm2.dump(), lokasi
examples.why: Every other entry keeps 'Circuit' (e.g. [21], [53], [56]), so 'sirkuit' here is inconsistent within the file. Starting the clause with 'mereka' for functions also reads a little like translationese.

examples.source: - Learn how to generate OpenQASM code in the [IBM Quantum Composer](/guides/composer) guide.
examples.translation: - Pelajari cara menghasilkan kode OpenQASM dalam panduan [IBM Quantum Composer](/guides/composer).
examples.suggested: - Pelajari cara menghasilkan kode OpenQASM dalam panduan [IBM Quantum Composer](/guides/composer).
examples.why: The English has no leading indentation here. Four-space indentation inside the admonition may make MDX render the list as a code block.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The ISA-circuit definition, the Batch/Session contrast and the Sampler (bitstrings) vs Estimator (expectation values) outputs all match the English, and nothing was added or dropped. A native editor would still fix a few phrasings. "postselection" became the reversed calque "seleksi pasca" where Indonesian uses "pascaseleksi". "Hadamard tests" became "tes Hadamard" where the usual technical term is "uji Hadamard". Entries [3] and [11] have stiff translationese, namely "komposabilitas yang mulus" and "mungkin juga diinginkan untuk menentukan".

examples.source: or postselection on inherent properties of the problem
examples.translation: atau seleksi pasca berdasarkan sifat bawaan dari masalah
examples.suggested: atau pascaseleksi berdasarkan sifat bawaan masalah
examples.why: 'seleksi pasca' copies the English word order backwards. Indonesian puts the prefix first: pascaseleksi (like 'pascaproses').

examples.source: inferring correlation functions using Hadamard tests
examples.translation: inferensi fungsi korelasi menggunakan tes Hadamard
examples.suggested: menginferensi fungsi korelasi menggunakan uji Hadamard
examples.why: Indonesian technical and scientific writing uses 'uji' for a test procedure. 'tes' sounds informal.

examples.source: it might also be desirable to specify the mapping of the problem onto qubits
examples.translation: mungkin juga diinginkan untuk menentukan pemetaan masalah ke qubit
examples.suggested: ada baiknya juga menentukan sejak awal pemetaan masalah ke qubit
examples.why: 'mungkin juga diinginkan untuk' is a word-for-word copy of the English passive and reads stiff. A native technical writer would say it more directly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Every limit keeps its number (10 juta eksekusi, 26,8 juta instruksi, 30/20 juta RZ/SX, lima juta Gate dua-Qubit) and the per-job, not per-PUB, caveat is kept. Three small edits remain. In [3], the hedge in "to try to ensure" is dropped, so validation sounds like a guarantee ("untuk memastikan"). In [15], "menangkap heuristik" copies the English "captures" word for word. In [18], a stray period was added inside the link text ("Backend kustom.").

examples.source: it is first validated to try to ensure that the job can run on the QPU
examples.translation: job tersebut pertama-tama divalidasi untuk memastikan bahwa job dapat berjalan di QPU
examples.suggested: job tersebut pertama-tama divalidasi untuk berusaha memastikan bahwa job dapat berjalan di QPU
examples.why: Dropping 'try to' makes the claim stronger, as if validation guarantees the job will run. The paragraph itself later says jobs may still fail.

examples.source: This table captures the heuristic used in validation
examples.translation: Tabel ini menangkap heuristik yang digunakan dalam validasi
examples.suggested: Tabel ini menggambarkan heuristik yang digunakan dalam validasi
examples.why: 'Menangkap' copies the English 'captures' word for word. 'Menggambarkan' or 'mencerminkan' is what an Indonesian technical writer would use.

examples.source: see [Transpile against custom backends](/guides/custom-backend#ex-count-ops).
examples.translation: lihat [Transpile terhadap Backend kustom.](/guides/custom-backend#ex-count-ops)
examples.suggested: lihat [Transpile terhadap Backend kustom](/guides/custom-backend#ex-count-ops).
examples.why: The sentence-final period was moved inside the link text, so the rendered link label ends with a period.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. Gate counts (ten times, three to four times), iteration counts (about 10 vs about 100), the local-search logic and the disclaimer caveat all match the English. The main slip is terminology: "entangling gates" becomes "gate yang berpilin" ("twisted gates") in [13] and [14]. That is an odd poetic calque a learner may not link to entanglement. Smaller calques are "dalam urutan sekitar 100 iterasi" for "on the order of" in [15], where "urutan" means sequence, and a trailing "masing-masing" in [24]. "infamous QAOA" is also flattened to "yang terkenal".

examples.source: use up to ten times fewer entangling gates than DQA
examples.translation: menggunakan hingga sepuluh kali lebih sedikit gate yang berpilin dibandingkan DQA
examples.suggested: menggunakan hingga sepuluh kali lebih sedikit gate entangling (gate pembentuk keterkaitan) dibandingkan DQA
examples.why: 'berpilin' means twisted/braided; it is not the conventional term, and a learner may not recognize it as entangling gates. The same rendering is used in [13].

examples.source: which is on the order of approximately 100 iterations
examples.translation: yang berada dalam urutan sekitar 100 iterasi
examples.suggested: yang umumnya memerlukan sekitar 100 iterasi (dalam orde 100 iterasi)
examples.why: 'urutan' means sequence/ordering. This calques 'order of magnitude' wrongly and reads stiffly.

examples.source: and $C^{*}$ is the cost of the best solution found, respectively
examples.translation: dan $C^{*}$ adalah biaya solusi terbaik yang ditemukan, masing-masing
examples.suggested: dan $C^{*}$ adalah biaya solusi terbaik yang ditemukan
examples.why: The trailing 'masing-masing' is an English calque of 'respectively' and reads unnaturally in Indonesian.

examples.source: the infamous QAOA algorithm
examples.translation: algoritma QAOA yang terkenal
examples.suggested: algoritma QAOA yang sudah sangat dikenal (dan kerap diperdebatkan)
examples.why: 'terkenal' neutralizes the slightly ironic 'infamous'. This is a small tone shift, not a factual error.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The retirement date, the roughly 50-qubit ceiling, the caveat in the Open Plan session warning and the note that local testing mode has no built-in mitigation are all kept intact, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. The one thing to fix is a term inconsistency. "Fake backend(s)" is kept as "fake backend" in [25], [28], [29] and [31], but the section heading [30] renders it as "Backend tiruan". A learner could miss that the heading introduces the same concept, so the heading should match the body text.

examples.source: Fake backends {#fake-backends}
examples.translation: Backend tiruan {#fake-backends}
examples.suggested: Fake backend {#fake-backends}
examples.why: Everywhere else in the file (for example [29] and [31]) the term stays as 'fake backend', so this heading is the only place it is translated. The heading should use the same term as the text below it.

editor_note: I found no misleading changes to meaning. Conditions, precedence rules and caveats all match the English: num_randomizations * shots_per_randomization "lebih diutamakan daripada" shots, the TREX exception is kept, "Parameter hilang karena sudah terikat ke nilai tetap" is right, and so is "Menjalankannya tetap memvalidasi". There are two small issues. The prose word "options" is split between "opsi" ([3], [8], [13], [29]) and the untranslated "options" ([17] "Pohon options", [20]/[22] "Kelas options"). In [53], two sentences in a row start with "Karena", which reads a bit stiffly.

examples.source: The options tree (`options.twirling`, ...)
examples.translation: Pohon options (`options.twirling`, ...)
examples.suggested: Pohon opsi (`options.twirling`, ...)
examples.why: In running prose, [3], [13] and [29] translate 'options' as 'opsi', but here and in the tables ('Kelas options') it stays in English. Use one form throughout.

examples.source: Thus, a realistic workload circuit can hang or exhaust memory. Since local testing only needs...
examples.translation: Karena itu, circuit workload yang realistis bisa hang atau menghabiskan memori. Karena pengujian lokal hanya perlu...
examples.suggested: Akibatnya, circuit workload yang realistis bisa hang atau menghabiskan memori. Karena pengujian lokal hanya perlu...
examples.why: Starting two sentences in a row with 'Karena' is clunky. Changing the first to 'Akibatnya' reads more naturally.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: the compatibility constraints ("hanya bekerja dengan `Estimator` sisi server versi lama"), the step 2 layer/Estimator positional-matching caveat, and the Pauli-Lindblad-only restriction in [38] all come through intact. "Sisi klien/sisi server", "model noise" and "box yang dianotasi" are used consistently.

The translation is faithful and natural, and it keeps the source's caveats: entry [7] keeps the stale-noise-model warning ("noise model akan kedaluwarsa setelah jangka waktu tertentu ... dalam satu session"), and entry [4] matches the English precision/shots claim, uses shots and Estimator consistently, and addresses the reader as Anda throughout.

The meaning is accurate throughout. The key teaching point stays intact: "In progress" time is not usage, and session mode is billed as elapsed time. Three small wording issues remain. "Plan" is rendered as "planmu" in [25] but as "paket/paketmu" in [27], and "paket" is also this page's word for software package ("Versi paket", "Paket provider"). "Usage" is kept in English in most places but becomes "sisa penggunaan" in heading [24]. The IQP tabs use the calque "Navigasikan ke" in [12], [27] and [31], while [38] and [42] use the more natural "Buka".

examples.source: Track how much of your plan's usage quota remains.
examples.translation: Lacak berapa banyak sisa kuota usage dari planmu.
examples.suggested: Lacak berapa banyak sisa kuota usage dari paket langgananmu.
examples.why: 'plan' is 'planmu' here but 'paketmu' in [27], and 'paket' also means software package on this page. Pick one term, such as 'paket langganan'.

examples.source: View remaining usage
examples.translation: Lihat sisa penggunaan
examples.suggested: Lihat sisa usage
examples.why: The rest of the file keeps 'usage' as a term (usage session, estimasi usage). Only this heading switches to 'penggunaan'.

examples.source: Navigate to the [Instances page] and select the tab...
examples.translation: Navigasikan ke [halaman Instances] dan pilih tab...
examples.suggested: Buka [halaman Instances] dan pilih tab...
examples.why: 'Navigasikan ke' is a calque of 'navigate to'. The file already uses the natural 'Buka [halaman Workloads]' in [38].

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. That includes the NoiseLearner/EstimatorV2 vs NoiseLearnerV3/Executor compatibility note in [8], the InjectNoise ref/modifier_ref explanation in [31], and the reason the two boxes have different refs in [32]. Two small things a native editor would fix. Entry [20] keeps the English word order in "ke IBM Quantum `EstimatorV2` primitive" and "Estimator primitive" instead of putting the head noun first ("primitive `EstimatorV2` dari IBM Quantum"). Entries [11] and [24] use "mengkarakterisasi" where standard Indonesian drops the k ("mengarakterisasi"). The register uses "kamu" consistently, and noise, laju error and lapisan are rendered the same way throughout the file.

examples.source: used as an input to the IBM Quantum `EstimatorV2` primitive
examples.translation: digunakan sebagai input ke IBM Quantum `EstimatorV2` primitive
examples.suggested: digunakan sebagai input ke primitive `EstimatorV2` dari IBM Quantum
examples.why: This copies the English modifier-before-noun order. In Indonesian the head noun comes first. The same pattern shows up in 'membuat instance Estimator primitive'.

examples.source: performs experiments that characterize noise processes
examples.translation: melakukan eksperimen yang mengkarakterisasi proses noise
examples.suggested: melakukan eksperimen yang mengarakterisasi proses noise
examples.why: Under the meN- prefix rule the initial k of 'karakterisasi' drops, giving 'mengarakterisasi'. The same form appears again in [24].

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, using informal "kamu" throughout; "thanks in part to its vibrant community" is correctly hedged as "sebagian berkat komunitasnya yang aktif dan bersemangat", and "Sumber terbuka" in headings next to "open-source" in the body is a defensible split.

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The tensor/expand subsystem ordering, the B.A vs A.B composition results, the global-phase caveat and the CP caveat all match the source, and 'kamu' is used throughout. Three phrasing slips are worth fixing. In [35], 'dikonversi menjadi satu' is a calque of 'converted into one' and reads like the number one. In [38], 'berbeda hanya berdasarkan fase global' is stiff. In [17], 'rangkaian Gate Pauli' uses 'rangkaian', which Indonesian readers also know as 'circuit', where 'urutan' would be clearer.

examples.source: it is implicitly converted into one by the method
examples.translation: ia akan secara implisit dikonversi menjadi satu oleh metode tersebut
examples.suggested: metode tersebut akan secara implisit mengonversinya menjadi objek Operator
examples.why: This is a calque of the English pronoun 'one'. In Indonesian, 'menjadi satu' reads as 'into a single one' or 'merged together'.

examples.source: two unitaries that differ by a global phase are not considered equal
examples.translation: dua uniter yang berbeda hanya berdasarkan fase global tidak dianggap sama
examples.suggested: dua uniter yang hanya berbeda fase global tidak dianggap sama
examples.why: 'berbeda berdasarkan' is stiff and doesn't sound natural. 'hanya berbeda fase global' is the idiomatic phrasing.

examples.source: converted into a sequence of single-qubit Pauli gates
examples.translation: dikonversi menjadi rangkaian Gate Pauli single-Qubit
examples.suggested: dikonversi menjadi urutan Gate Pauli single-Qubit
examples.why: 'rangkaian' is also the standard Indonesian word for 'circuit', so on a page about inserting operators into circuits it is ambiguous. 'urutan' clearly means sequence.

editor_note: I checked the meaning entry by entry and found nothing that would mislead a learner. The QAOA explanation, the benchmark caveats, the MS-violation definition and the spin-mapping example all match the English. Four small wording issues remain. The product name appears three ways: "Fungsi Qiskit" in [1], [35] and [56], "Qiskit Functions" in [4], and "function ini" / "Qiskit Function ini" in [62]. "Ground state" is written "keadaan dasar (ground state)" in [9] but left in English in [21]. [37] has a redundant "Pertama ... terlebih dahulu", and [26] has the calque "seberapa jauh solusi dari memenuhi semua batasan".

examples.source: Request access to the function ... for this Qiskit Function.
examples.translation: Minta akses ke function ini ... untuk Qiskit Function ini.
examples.suggested: Minta akses ke fungsi ini ... untuk Fungsi Qiskit ini.
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'Fungsi Qiskit'. Here the English 'function' / 'Qiskit Function' comes back, so the name is inconsistent.

examples.source: leads to exact ground states
examples.translation: menghasilkan ground state yang tepat
examples.suggested: menghasilkan keadaan dasar yang eksak
examples.why: [9] already introduced 'keadaan dasar (ground state)', so this entry should use the same term. 'eksak' also matches how 'exact' is rendered in [32].

examples.source: The problem is first defined by using a dictionary:
examples.translation: Pertama, masalah didefinisikan terlebih dahulu menggunakan dictionary:
examples.suggested: Pertama, masalah didefinisikan menggunakan dictionary:
examples.why: 'Pertama' and 'terlebih dahulu' both mean 'first', so the sentence says it twice.

examples.source: measures how far the solution is from satisfying all constraints
examples.translation: mengukur seberapa jauh solusi dari memenuhi semua batasan
examples.suggested: mengukur seberapa jauh solusi belum memenuhi semua batasan
examples.why: 'jauh ... dari memenuhi' copies the English 'far from satisfying' word for word and reads stiffly in Indonesian.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally in the informal "kamu" register, and every plan detail is kept exactly: "minimal 400" minutes, "lebih dari 10.000 menit" as the Premium threshold, "hingga 10 menit per jendela bergulir 28 hari", and the us-east-only limit for Open Plan instances.

I found no meaning drift. The broadcasting rules [18]-[26], the 5x1/1x6/4x6/3x6 examples [29]-[32] and the note that commuting observables in different PUBs are measured separately [10] all match the English. A few small wording problems remain. "Commuting" is rendered with the loanword "(saling) komuting", where "saling berkomutasi" reads more naturally. "Standard deviation" appears as "deviasi standar" in [41] but "standar deviasi" in [47]. [56] leaves "dictionary of counts" as a half-English calque, and [51] renders "runs over" as the stiff "berjalan melalui".

examples.source: If you have two commuting observables in different PUBs
examples.translation: dua observable yang saling komuting di PUB berbeda
examples.suggested: dua observable yang saling berkomutasi di PUB berbeda
examples.why: 'komuting' is an unadapted loanword. 'berkomutasi' is the usual Indonesian verb form.

examples.source: associated standard deviations
examples.translation: standar deviasi terkait
examples.suggested: deviasi standar terkait
examples.why: [41] uses 'deviasi standar'. The file should use one form, and 'deviasi standar' is the standard one.

examples.source: rather than on dictionaries of counts
examples.translation: daripada pada dictionary of counts
examples.suggested: daripada pada dictionary hasil hitungan (counts)
examples.why: Leaving the English phrase 'dictionary of counts' in the middle of the sentence is a half-translated calque.

examples.source: The left-most axis of this array runs over ordered shots, while the right-most axis runs over bytes.
examples.translation: Sumbu paling kiri dari array ini berjalan melalui shot yang terurut, sementara sumbu paling kanan berjalan melalui byte.
examples.suggested: Sumbu paling kiri array ini mengindeks shot secara berurutan, sedangkan sumbu paling kanan mengindeks byte.
examples.why: 'berjalan melalui' is a literal rendering of 'runs over'. 'mengindeks' states the array-axis meaning clearly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. Estimator/Sampler, "nilai ekspektasi" and the abstraction-layer argument all carry over correctly. There are three small slips. In [7], "would not and should not be familiar" becomes "tidak perlu dan tidak harus memahami", which softens the normative "should not" to "doesn't have to". In [28], the link text uses "primitif" while the rest of the file keeps "primitives/primitive". A few phrases are calqued: "lebih sedikit pada detail hardware" in [16] and "menghasilkan hasil" in [28].

editor_note: Faithful and natural, with every deprecation date and version kept intact (deprecated→"tidak digunakan lagi … akan dihapus pada awal 2025", "Qiskit SDK v1.3.0 … v2.0.0"), and terms used the same way throughout (fractional gates, kontrol tingkat pulse, kalibrasi, "Anda" register).

Nothing here would mislead a learner, but the terminology needs tidying. The page mostly renders "constrained/unconstrained" as "terkendali/tidak terkendali", which reads as "controlled/uncontrolled". It switches to the correct "terkendala" only in [55] and [62]. It also mixes simpul/node, tepi/edge, "suku penalti"/"penalty term" and "kendala"/"hard constraint(s)" between [12]/[28] and [45]-[58]. In [50], "biarkan" is a word-for-word calque of mathematical "let" where Indonesian uses "misalkan".

examples.source: Example: Unconstrained optimization
examples.translation: Contoh: Optimasi tidak terkendali
examples.suggested: Contoh: Optimasi tanpa kendala
examples.why: 'tidak terkendali' means 'uncontrolled / out of control'. The standard term for constrained/unconstrained optimization is 'terkendala / tanpa kendala', which the file itself uses in [55] and [62].

examples.source: Both unconstrained and constrained problems are solvable, with constraints enforced as hard Hamming-weight-1 constraints rather than penalty terms.

examples.why: This entry uses 'suku penalti', but [45]/[54] use 'penalty term'. It uses 'simpul' here and in [32]/[48], but [46]/[50]/[52] use 'node'. The same concepts are split across Indonesian and English renderings.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Every caveat survives: the "not eligible for execution on hardware" limits in notes 8 and 9, the July 2025 / qiskit-qasm3-import v0.6.0 limits in notes 4, 6 and 7, and the Python-space admonition. Two wording slips remain. In note 5, the parser "resolving" `let` alias statements comes out as "menyelesaikan", which reads as "finish/solve"; "menguraikan" or "me-resolve" is the usual technical choice. In note 2, "parsing dan dumping" leaves "dumping" as raw English even though the page's own term for `dumps` elsewhere is "diekspor/ekspor".

examples.source: The Qiskit OpenQASM 3 parser can resolve `let` alias statements that bind the result of register concantenation.

editor_note: No meaning is lost. The removals, the caveats (for example that `None` is returned when no properties are set, and the v1.x support dates) and the migration paths all match the English, and the informal "kamu" register is consistent. A few spots read as stiff or ambiguous. In [22], "indeks Target pertama" can be read as "the first Target index" when the English means "index the Target first", and "mengquery" is an awkward hybrid verb. In [37], "dengan cepat dengan error" repeats "dengan". In [20], "bahkan" has moved, so the sentence stresses the slowdown instead of saying that even operations that never touch the data got slower.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The authentication caveats in [38] and [23] carry over correctly, and so does the reinforcement-learning description in [29]. editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing would mislead a learner. The page switches address register: the body uses "Anda", but the headings and [31] use the informal suffix "-mu" ("penyedia ID-mu", "firewall-mu", "firewall-mu agar"). editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. The IBM-versus-user split of responsibilities is kept exactly, including the disclaimer "IBM tidak bertanggung jawab atas pencadangan atau pemulihan data workload pengguna", and the terms are rendered consistently: "Tanggung jawabmu", "ketersediaan tinggi", "data saat transit" and "dienkripsi dari ujung ke ujung".

The meaning holds throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are a few spots of stiff or inconsistent wording. "Vectorized" appears as "tervektorisasi" in [6] but stays English as "vectorized" in [12], which also doubles up with "satu objek ... tunggal". [16] calques "runs over" as "berjalan di atas", and [23] renders "dictionaries of counts" as the awkward "dictionary jumlah". editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The Sampler V2 caveat in [21] ("tidak mendukung penentuan tingkat resilience") and the Open Plan restriction in [35] ("tidak dapat mengirimkan job sesi") both carry over correctly. Two phrasings are stiff. In [14], "SamplerV2 mengambil ... sebagai input" copies the English "takes"; "menerima" is the natural Indonesian verb here. In [35], "Berlatih dengan primitif dengan mengerjakan" repeats "dengan" and reads clumsily. editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally in the informal "kamu" register. The serializable-input caveat [27], the magic-command caution [24] and the get_runtime_service linkage explanation [31] all come through intact. editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout, with the details that matter kept exactly: the 16 inti CPU / 32 GB RAM allocation, the 1024-byte memory arithmetic, the "Hanya file `tar` dan `h5`" and flat `/data` limits, and "alokasi pecahan" for fractional CPU allocation. The informal "kamu" register is used consistently.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The 50–100-qubit limit, the angle set {0, π/2, π, 3π/2}, the 2% depolarizing and 5% readout noise figures, and the "Pauli channels only" caveat all come through intact, and the "kamu" register is used consistently. There are two small phrasing issues a native editor would fix. In [21], "hasilnya sangat mungkin adalah 0" is a word-for-word calque with a stray "adalah". In [13], "mendapatkan keyakinan" is stiff and should become "menjadi lebih yakin".

examples.suggested: Karena struktur khusus Circuit stabilizer, hasilnya kemungkinan besar 0.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The 2% depolarizing error on CX, the (1 - p)^m reasoning, the conservative 65% estimate and the need to add measurements before running Sampler all match the English, and terms are consistent (nilai harapan, keadaan tercampur, model noise). Two small edits would help. In [16], "Setelah $m$ aplikasi depolarizing channel" copies the English "m applications" word for word; an Indonesian writer would say the channel is applied m times. In [14], "mempengaruhi" should use the KBBI standard spelling "memengaruhi".

examples.source: After $m$ applications of the depolarizing channel, the probability of the state being preserved would be $(1 - p)^m$.

examples.suggested: Untuk mendapat gambaran kasar tentang bagaimana noise memengaruhi hasil akhir

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The key constraints are kept: the Estimator input must not contain measurements ("tidak boleh ... pengukuran"), the Sampler input must contain them ("harus"), and precision is set only in .run(). The issues are small. "Circuit" is rendered two ways: the two measurement notes [12] and [33] use "sirkuit" while every other entry keeps "Circuit". [26] and [43] calque "introduce the effect" as "memperkenalkan efek", and "memberikan efek" or "menambahkan efek" reads more naturally. The pronoun "Ia" is used for a class in [10] and [30], which sounds stiff; "Kelas ini" is more natural.

examples.translation: Ia dapat menerima Circuit, observable, dan parameter sebagai input

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and the exclusive=true/false lane semantics in [35]-[36] and the credential caveats in [28] are faithful. In [32], "tidak ada penjadwalan pengguna lain di luar Slurm" can be read as "no scheduling of other users" instead of "no other scheduling mechanism for users". It needs light rewording but does not mislead. There are two stylistic slips. [44] calques "under which user and service instance" as "di bawah pengguna dan instance layanan mana". The heading [21] renders "Backend specifics" as "Spesifikasi Backend", which reads as "Backend specification".

examples.source: there is no other scheduling of users involved outside of Slurm
examples.translation: tidak ada penjadwalan pengguna lain di luar Slurm
examples.suggested: tidak ada mekanisme penjadwalan lain untuk pengguna di luar Slurm
examples.why: The word order attaches 'lain' to 'pengguna' ('other users'), so the sentence is ambiguous. The source means there is no other scheduling mechanism.

examples.source: These details determine under which user and service instance IBM Quantum Compute Service is used.
examples.translation: Detail ini menentukan di bawah pengguna dan instance layanan mana IBM Quantum Compute Service digunakan.
examples.suggested: Detail ini menentukan atas nama pengguna dan instance layanan mana IBM Quantum Compute Service digunakan.
examples.why: 'di bawah ... mana' is a stiff calque of the English 'under which'. 'atas nama' is the natural Indonesian phrasing.

examples.source: Backend specifics
examples.translation: Spesifikasi Backend
examples.suggested: Ketentuan khusus per Backend
examples.why: 'Spesifikasi' means technical specification. The section actually covers backend-specific setup details.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Every constraint in the limitations list (one stretch per qubit set, no negative delays, the X*stretch + Y form) keeps its negation and scope, and the remainder, 1365+10 and billing caveats are all intact. There are two small wording issues. In [3], "higher-order echo decoupling" becomes "tingkat tinggi", where the usual term is "orde lebih tinggi". Also in [3], "left-aligning" is left as an English gerund in the middle of an Indonesian list, even though [11] already renders it naturally as "disejajarkan ke kiri".

examples.source: to implement a higher-order echo decoupling sequence
examples.translation: untuk mengimplementasikan urutan echo decoupling tingkat tinggi
examples.suggested: untuk mengimplementasikan urutan echo decoupling orde lebih tinggi
examples.why: 'Higher-order' refers to the order of the sequence, so the usual Indonesian term is 'orde (lebih) tinggi'. 'Tingkat tinggi' suggests 'advanced' or 'high-level'.

examples.source: left-aligning a sequence of gates
examples.translation: left-aligning urutan gate
examples.suggested: menyejajarkan urutan gate ke kiri
examples.why: An English gerund in the middle of an Indonesian list is jarring, and entry [11] already uses 'disejajarkan ke kiri' for the same idea.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the technical M3 description in [26] ("faktorisasi LU langsung atau metode iteratif terprakondisi ... konvergen dalam O(1) langkah") and the "not part of Qiskit itself" caveat in [5] and [22]. Nothing here would mislead a learner. The address form switches partway through the page. Entries [4] and [16] use "Anda", then [18] and [27] switch to "Kamu"/"proyekmu", so one short page speaks to the reader in two different ways. A smaller point: the term is "Addon Qiskit" in the heading [19] but "Qiskit addons" in the running prose of [20], which leaves the English word order and plural in Indonesian text.

examples.source: You can now use the Benchpress package to perform your own analysis of quantum SDK performance.
examples.translation: Kamu sekarang bisa menggunakan paket Benchpress untuk melakukan analisis sendiri terhadap performa SDK kuantum.
examples.suggested: Anda sekarang bisa menggunakan paket Benchpress untuk melakukan analisis sendiri terhadap performa SDK kuantum.
examples.why: Entries [4] and [16] address the reader as 'Anda'. Switching to 'Kamu' partway through the page is inconsistent.

examples.source: You can find a catalog of projects in the Qiskit ecosystem page, as well as information about how to nominate your own project.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa menemukan katalog proyek di halaman ekosistem Qiskit, serta informasi tentang cara menominasikan proyekmu sendiri.
examples.suggested: Anda bisa menemukan katalog proyek di halaman ekosistem Qiskit, serta informasi tentang cara menominasikan proyek Anda sendiri.
examples.why: This is the same Anda/kamu inconsistency within the page.

examples.source: Qiskit addons are a collection of research capabilities...
examples.translation: Qiskit addons adalah kumpulan kemampuan penelitian ...
examples.suggested: Addon Qiskit adalah kumpulan kemampuan penelitian ...
examples.why: This keeps the English plural and word order. The heading [19] already uses the natural Indonesian form 'Addon Qiskit'.
